finalRecapture.scope: All twelve existing mutations tied to the two edited Codex property files were detected, replayed and restored against their updated propertySha256 sources. Two new mutations prove distinct-tail retention and exact model scope. The remaining five Codex and eleven Claude mutations retain their unchanged source hashes.

commands.family: cd apps/desktop && pnpm exec vitest run tests/property/codex-*.property.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 (filter by file path rather than by `-t <family>`, which silently drops properties whose test name lacks the family word; a path handed to `pnpm test:properties -- <path>` also runs the whole suite, because the wrapper always passes tests/property as its first filter and vitest unions the filters)
commands.explore: cd apps/desktop && FC_EXPLORE=1 pnpm exec vitest run tests/property/codex-*.property.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
commands.mutationDetect: FC_RUNS=<runs> FC_SEED=<seed> pnpm --dir apps/desktop exec vitest run tests/property/<file> --maxWorkers=1 -t '<selector>'
commands.mutationReplay: FC_RUNS=<numRuns> FC_SEED=<seed> FC_PATH='<path>' pnpm --dir apps/desktop exec vitest run tests/property/<file> --maxWorkers=1 -t '<selector>'

samples.codex-state.property.test.ts: the state-machine invariant, tail-truncation and delta-batch properties keep 50 normal / 500 exploration (reduced from the 100/1000 pure tier for the ≤10 s cost gate); the 200-turn truncation window property keeps 30/100 because each sample stages MAX_TURNS + 1 rounds. The state-machine property asserts a per-event expected effect (the owned mutation of each native event type) before the general invariants, so a reducer case that silently drops its own field fails even when the remaining state stays internally consistent. A mandatory 230-step plan example opens the state-machine property, so the reducer's 200-step head-keeping plan slice is exercised on every run — the generated domain never reaches the cap. Mandatory entity-lifecycle examples open an activity, an interaction that blocks its turn and a Primary Session so each close/progress event is retargeted at the live entity it closes and the resulting status change is asserted, including the waiting-input → running resume of the last blocking interaction, whose expected status is derived from the pre-state and the closed id; the session branch additionally asserts the accepted event's binding directly, since that binding is the event's only observable effect and observe skips the monotonicity check when the reducer returns the prior object. The same targeted examples pin the four effect details the generated domain leaves implicit: an activity-update must stamp the turn's updatedAt, an activity-end must leave a live target terminalized and an unknown target's activity list untouched, an interaction-closed must map the resolution to its exact persisted status rather than a generic one, and a done event must settle former streaming assistant items to the outcome-specific status. Mandatory resolution and outcome examples (eight interaction resolutions, three done outcomes, each rewinding a single step of the entity-lifecycle scenario) keep those mappings on every run. The delta-batch property reduces each delta on its own and again through the production mergeDeltaEvents exported from main/thread/thread-handle.ts, so a lossy production batcher fails the equivalence instead of a test-local reimplementation passing it
samples.codex-jsonlines.property.test.ts: 100 normal / 1000 exploration; opens with a mandatory example that pushes 中🙂文 one byte at a time through an unterminated stream
samples.codex-interaction.property.test.ts: 100 normal / 1000 exploration per property; mandatory examples open one sample per native method, and every admitted interaction's advertised action ids are compared against an independently declared expected set per method (commandExecution/fileChange approvals: allow-once, allow-session, deny, cancel; permissions approval: allow-once, allow-session, deny; tool requestUserInput: submit, cancel; mcpServer elicitation: submit, deny, cancel), so a dropped action fails even though every remaining action still encodes; question ids stay distinct inside one request, because the public contract requires unique question ids and a repeated native id is refused fail-closed at admission instead of projected
samples.codex-bart-usage.property.test.ts: 100 normal / 1000 exploration per property; provider/model id spaces may overlap so the primary bucket's insert-only precedence stays reachable, a mandatory overlap example carries one limit id in both buckets with distinguishable quotas on every run, a second mandatory example pins a dictionary bucket that shadows the frame's primary id and carries the reach flag with no recognizable window (the frame reports the explicit reach, not the tri-state fold over an empty provider window list), and every window's percentage, positive-only duration and ISO-or-omitted reset timestamp are compared against the input-derived expectation; the scope and limitReached oracles read the resolved bucket map, so a shadowing dictionary bucket contributes its own provider-scoped flags
samples.codex-tool-identity.property.test.ts: 100 normal / 1000 exploration per property; key-order permutations recurse through object-valued members and nested arrays, and the generated domain is backed by mandatory examples: a nested object whose inner key order is reversed, and a two-binding tool whose bindings are swapped. Binding swaps are therefore exercised on every run rather than only when a generated injection happens to contain two distinct bindings.

cost.method: Final local review remeasured three alternating whole-suite baseline/candidate pairs, three Codex exploration runs and three per-file runs for each of the two edited properties, using the propertySha256 sources above. Every wall measurement includes registry generation followed by one Vitest process with --maxWorkers=1. The three unchanged Codex files retain their preceding per-file wall measurements; test body times are sums of assertion durations from the final whole-suite candidate run. Measurements were sequential on the user's active Mac; wall times include ambient load.
cost.exploration: Final source hashes passed FC_EXPLORE=1 in all three Codex family runs (5 files / 14 tests): 9.77 / 9.61 / 12.30 s wall, median 9.77 s, including registry generation. The three heavy state properties use 500 samples, the 200-turn property 100, and other properties 1000. Each of the fourteen recaptured mutations also passed its normal-tier replay after byte-exact production restore; the two new mutations cover head retention and model-to-feature scope regression.
cost.gate: Three alternating whole-suite pairs include check.test.ts in both legs: baseline 16 files / 100 tests at 67.04 / 71.44 / 95.23 s, candidate 25 files / 125 tests at 70.62 / 72.71 / 79.21 s. Median difference 1.27 s; same-round differences 3.58 / 1.27 / -16.02 s. This is within the <=10 s-per-phase gate. The nine new files add 25 tests.

limitations: Pure in-process properties only: no subprocess, OS scheduling, storage or filesystem ordering is generated. Native Handle behavior stays with native-harness.property.test.ts; settings merges stay with harness-settings.property.test.ts. Every checkAsync property name equals its outer vitest it() title, and the recorded selector per fault is that shared title, so generated replay commands select exactly one test; a name that was not a substring of its it() title (as earlier revisions of these files had) would silently select nothing. Mutation runs used the tier recorded in each fault's detection block (30 for the 200-turn truncation window, 50 for the codex-state properties, 100 elsewhere) with the failing seed pinned, so re-running the recorded mutationDetect command reproduces the recorded detect log and counterexample exactly and the recorded mutationReplay command reproduces it at 0 additional shrink steps. Detection seeds are drawn from the recorded runs and are negative for some faults, which fast-check accepts. The families' normal tier is 100 except codex-state's three heaviest properties (50) and its 200-turn truncation window property (30). toolConfigurationIdentity's generated keys stay in a safe ASCII range because localeCompare ties would re-expose insertion order; percentValue's honest domain is non-negative with two-decimal rounding (values above 100 pass through by design). The raw detect/replay/restored logs live under the gitignored .agents/local/property-faults/ scratch area, so only their SHA-256 digests travel with the repo; each digest covers the full vitest output for that stage. Every mutation was removed by restoring the exact original source bytes (SHA-256 verified against the pre-mutation digest, which is the hash of the file as delivered); no runtime fault switch is retained. The recorded propertySha256 values are the hashes of the delivered files at the time of this capture, so a later edit to a property file invalidates them and the evidence must be recaptured.

jsonLinesRecapture.note: Only the relocated JSON Lines family was recaptured here; other mutation records retain their original capture provenance. The public plugin-kit/main import resolves dist, so rebuild plugin-kit after applying each source mutation and again after byte-exact restoration, before detection, replay, or clean replay.
